mainEntity.name: How much does a Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A full rebuilt Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue engine typically costs between £2,500 and £4,000 for supply only, while used units start from around £600.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue engine replacement take?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the T8CC and T9CB engine codes in the Ford S-Max?

acceptedAnswer.text: The T8CC code is the standard 2.0-litre EcoBlue diesel producing 177PS, favoured for Zetec and Titanium trims, while the T9CB code is a Bi-Turbo variant producing an increased output of 207PS for Titanium Sport and ST-Line models.

mainEntity.name: Has there been a recall for the Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue AdBlue or DPF issues?

acceptedAnswer.text: While there have been widespread reports of AdBlue crystallization and DPF regeneration issues across the EcoBlue range, there is currently no official UK-wide recall specifically for the S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue.

commonProblems.h2: Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue is a highly capable, refined diesel unit, but its complex emissions and timing systems are not immune to wear. The T8CC and T9CB codes dominate replacement demand for this variant due to AdBlue contamination and EGR/DPF failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: AdBlue System Crystallization & EGR Clogging - Why the Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue (T8CC/T9CB) Fails Emissions
problems.rootCause: AdBlue fluid crystallizes inside the tank and pump, blocking the injector and triggering a "Engine Fault: Restart Not Possible" warning. Concurrently, exhaust gases recirculated by the EGR valve deposit heavy carbon soot, restricting airflow.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace AdBlue tank/pump, clean EGR, reset ECU adaptations.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if caught early before internal engine contamination occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: The right call only if AdBlue contamination has caused catastrophic internal cylinder or bearing corrosion.

problems.recommendation: For Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue owners, AdBlue and EGR system failures are highly common but often repairable without requiring a full engine replacement, provided the issue is caught before internal corrosion occurs. However, if the engine has suffered severe DPF-related turbo starvation or catastrophic internal wear, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine is the most reliable long-term solution to preserve the vehicle's heavy-duty MPV capabilities.

problems.h4: DPF Regeneration Failure & Turbo Wear - Why the Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue (T9CB) Loses Power
problems.rootCause: Urban driving prevents the DPF from completing active regeneration cycles. The resulting backpressure can starve the twin-turbo setup of proper airflow, leading to limp mode and potential turbocharger damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Chemical DPF clean, turbo actuator inspection, and ECU reset.
repairOptions.longevity: Suitable if the turbo core is undamaged and no debris has entered the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded components addressing the original failure point, 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if DPF blockage has caused turbo failure or if compression is compromised.

items.question: What are the common signs of Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue engine failure?
items.answer: Owners of the Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue should watch for a "Restart Not Possible" AdBlue warning, excessive black smoke from the exhaust, or a noticeable loss of power under acceleration.
keyPoints: A persistent limp mode often indicates severe DPF clogging or turbo actuator failure.
If the engine management light is flashing alongside these symptoms, stop driving immediately.
Continuing to drive can cause catastrophic internal damage to the turbocharger or engine block.

items.question: What is the difference between the T8CC and T9CB engine codes in the Ford S-Max?
items.answer: The T8CC code is the standard 2.0-litre EcoBlue diesel producing 177PS, favoured for Zetec and Titanium trims, while the T9CB code is a Bi-Turbo variant producing an increased output of 207PS for Titanium Sport and ST-Line models.
keyPoints: Although they share the same 2.0L EcoBlue architecture, their turbocharger setups and ECU mappings differ significantly.
Swapping them requires careful verification of compatibility, especially regarding the turbo and intercooler piping.
Always verify your exact engine code via your V5C logbook or registration before ordering a replacement.

items.question: Has there been a recall for the Ford S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue AdBlue or DPF issues?
items.answer: While there have been widespread reports of AdBlue crystallization and DPF regeneration issues across the EcoBlue range, there is currently no official UK-wide recall specifically for the S-Max 2.0 EcoBlue.
keyPoints: Ford has issued internal Service Special Messages (SSM) to dealers regarding AdBlue system contamination.
Preventative AdBlue system flushing and using high-quality diesel are strongly recommended.
If your system has already failed catastrophically, a full engine replacement is often the only viable solution.
